h1: Shantaa Koh Kood — Hillside Sea-View Villas Above Ao Tapao That Keep Guests Coming Back
intro: On a green hillside above Ao Tapao on Koh Kood's west coast sits a boutique resort that tucks its villas through the forest across roughly 35 rai of land — Shantaa Koh Kood. What guests mention most is the quiet and the sea views from up on the slope. The resort has been family-run since 2004 and deliberately keeps guest numbers low so it feels like you have space to yourself. Room types range from the twin-queen Shantaa Villa for families to the Shantaa Sweet, designed for couples who want calm, many with outdoor jungle bathrooms. There's an infinity pool looking out to sea, a sea-view restaurant, and free kayaks and surfboards. From approx. ฿4,500/night, scoring 9.4 from around 385 reviews. It suits couples and anyone after a restful, private stay — just know the beach in front is a small rocky one, and the villas sit on a slope you'll walk up and down.

body.html: Shantaa Koh Kood sits on a hillside above Ao Tapao on the west coast of Koh Kood, Trat, across roughly 35 rai of land. What sets it apart from the usual beachfront resort is the way the villas are spread out through the forest on the slope, giving each one real privacy and many of them a view out to sea from up high. The resort has been family-run since 2004, deliberately keeps guest numbers low, and is staffed largely by local Koh Kood residents. TripAdvisor ranks it #1 of 17 hotels on Koh Kood with a 4.9 score from over 600 reviews, which says a lot about how guests feel about the place overall.

There are several room types to match group size and budget. Shantaa Villa has twin queen beds and sleeps up to three, good for families or groups of friends. Shantaa Sweet is a king-bed room built for two, the choice for couples who want quiet, while Extra Sweet and Extra Sweet PLUS are larger versions that take children too. A detail many reviews single out is the outdoor bathrooms ringed by jungle — you shower to the sound of the forest. To be straight: some room categories feel fairly compact for the price and lean toward simple, nature-led styling rather than slick new luxury, so look at the size and photos of each type before you book.

"We woke up to a sea view from the hill, so quiet you only hear birds and the waves. The breakfast is freshly made and genuinely good, and staff knew our names from day one. The place is big but with few guests it feels like you have it to yourselves."

The charm of Shantaa is that it's large but uncrowded, with staff who look after you personally. Plenty of reviews praise the freshly made breakfast and good coffee, along with dinners at the sea-view restaurant. There's an infinity pool that looks out to the sea, the Ghati cafe for a slow coffee, a beach bar, and a spa. The resort lends out kayaks and surfboards for free, and there are several small beaches around the grounds to swim from. The overall mood leans toward adult tranquility, so it fits people coming to rest quietly more than families travelling with several small children.

Two things are worth being honest about before you book. First, the beach and the hillside setting — the beach in front is a small rocky one, not a long white-sand stretch like Klong Chao, so for proper sand you'll walk or take a ride to another spot, and because the villas sit on a slope you'll handle ramps and steps between your room, the pool and the restaurant, which may not suit older guests or anyone who struggles with stairs. Second, the nature of Koh Kood itself — the island is still wild, with no big convenience stores or nightlife, the kitchen closes fairly early in the evening, and getting here from Bangkok means a drive to the Trat piers then a 1–1.5 hour speedboat to the island, followed by another transfer to Ao Tapao.

The upside of being on the hill is views and privacy that a beachfront resort can't give you. Many guests say the sea view from the balcony and the infinity pool is well worth the climb, and the quiet up the slope means better sleep than a room beside a busy path. The resort suggests renting a scooter to get around the island, since Ao Tapao is quiet and a fair way from the main dining cluster at Klong Chao. The resort scores 9.4 from around 385 Agoda reviews and as high as 9.7 on Booking.com from over 700 guests, reflecting how much people enjoy the atmosphere, the service and that breakfast.

The honest bottom line: Shantaa Koh Kood is best for couples and travellers who want a quiet resort on a sea-view hillside, plenty of space with few guests, a good breakfast and warm, personal service. What you have to accept is the small rocky beach in front, the climb up and down the slope, and rooms that can feel compact for the price, plus the realities of Koh Kood — multiple transfers to get here and an early kitchen close. If you weight quiet, views and service most heavily, this place delivers well enough to sit at #1 on the island.

Tips from following the reviews here for a while: ask for a villa with a sea view that sits at a level you can walk to easily — flag it when you book, because the view from the hill is the real draw. If there are two of you, choose the Shantaa Sweet, which is built for couples; families should go for the Shantaa Villa or Extra Sweet PLUS. Try the outdoor jungle bathroom, a real signature here. Rent a scooter to head out for meals and to reach the waterfalls and other beaches around the island, since Ao Tapao is quiet. High season (November–April) brings the clearest water and best weather — book ahead and lock a free-cancellation rate. During the rains (May–October) much of Koh Kood closes, so check opening dates and boat schedules before you plan.

If you have trouble walking, or travel with older guests or several small children — the villas are on a slope, with ramps and steps between your room, the pool and the restaurant → tell the resort when you book to request a room at a level that's easiest to reach, and know the mood leans adult.

If you're coming in the rainy season (May–Oct) — many Koh Kood resorts and shops close, boats run less often, the water can be cloudy, and the forest is humid → check opening dates and boat schedules with the resort before booking, and pick a free-cancellation rate.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Shantaa Koh Kood

faq.q: Where is Shantaa Koh Kood and how do you get there?
faq.a: The resort sits on a hillside above Ao Tapao on the west coast of Koh Kood, Trat, across roughly 35 rai of land. From Bangkok you drive to the Trat piers (Laem Sok or Laem Ngop), take a 1–1.5 hour speedboat to Koh Kood, then transfer to Ao Tapao. Ao Tapao is fairly quiet and a way from the main dining cluster at Klong Chao, so renting a scooter to get around the island is recommended.

faq.q: What does Shantaa cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at approx. ฿4,500/night for the Shantaa Sweet, a king-bed room for couples. Above that are the twin-queen Shantaa Villa for families, plus the larger Extra Sweet and Extra Sweet PLUS, which sleeps up to four. Prices vary by date and package and climb quickly in high season, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What's the beach like in front of Shantaa — is it good for sand lovers?
faq.a: The beach in front is a small rocky one, not a long white-sand stretch. Shantaa's draw is the sea view from the hillside and the quiet, not stepping straight onto sand. For a wide sandy beach you'll ride to Klong Chao or another beach on the island. It suits people who weight views, calm and service over sand.

It's best for couples and travellers who want a quiet resort on a sea-view hillside, plenty of space with few guests, a good breakfast and warm, personal service. The mood leans toward adult tranquility, and it ranks #1 of 17 hotels on Koh Kood on TripAdvisor. Families can stay too, but should be ready for the walking up and down the slope.

faq.q: Are the villas on a slope — is there a lot of walking, and what should I know?
faq.a: The villas are spread across a forested hillside, so you'll walk up and down ramps and steps between your room, the pool and the restaurant. It may not suit older guests or anyone who struggles with stairs — tell the resort at booking to request a room at a level that's easiest to reach. The trade-off is sea views and a privacy a beachfront resort can't offer.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book and when's the best time to go?
faq.a: The best time on Koh Kood is high season (November–April), with the clearest water and best weather. The resort keeps guest numbers low and fills up, so book 3–6 weeks ahead. In the rainy season (May–October) the island is quiet, many resorts and shops close, boats run less often and the forest is humid, so check opening dates and boat schedules first. Pick a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm.
